page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-16-lssd is a general-purpose server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The system is equipped with 64 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4 GB of memory per core. Storage is bundled as a single local NVMe SSD with a capacity of 402 GB, while no dedicated GPU hardware is present.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU capabilities, with stress-ng single-core performance and Geekbench text processing scoring in the top 25%. Multi-core CPU performance, software compilation, and cryptography operations fall within the average range. However, memory bandwidth presents a notable bottleneck; while cached small-block reads are average, uncached large-block read and write memory bandwidth scores in the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively.

This hardware profile is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, static web serving, and database operations that benefit from local NVMe storage. It handles small to medium language model inference at average speeds, though large-scale LLM inference is highly constrained, with prompt processing for 70B models falling into the bottom 10%. The instance offers a balanced resource density for applications requiring dedicated AMD EPYC compute power paired with fast local scratch space, though memory-intensive workloads requiring high uncached bandwidth may experience performance limitations.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-16-lssd is a general-purpose server configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor, 64 GB of RAM, and a 402 GB local NVMe SSD. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, this instance delivers strong single-core CPU performance and text processing capabilities, ranking in the top 25% of benchmarks. Multi-core execution, database operations, and web serving throughput remain average. A key hardware tradeoff is its uncached memory bandwidth, which performs poorly under large-block read and write tests. Lacking a GPU, it is not designed for heavy graphics or large-scale AI workloads, as demonstrated by poor performance on 70B LLM prompt processing. It is best suited for general-purpose applications, software compilation, and database tasks that leverage its local NVMe storage.
